name: Essential Utilities, Inc.
share_adj_basis: applied to revenue components only (v5.4); OE/share CAGR enters unadjusted

overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0000078128-26-000050), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Property, plant and equipment additions, including the debt component of allowance for funds used during construction': $(1,429,980) thousand for FY2025, $(1,329,747) thousand for FY2024 and $(1,199,103) thousand for FY2023; the identical three figures are reported as consolidated capital expenditures in the same 10-K's segment note (Note 19) and are tagged in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings. The override value is the median of the three filed years.
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because Essential Utilities files its capital expenditures on the cash-flow line 'Property, plant and equipment additions' tagged us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings, which is not in the engine's candidate tag list (the engine's PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment series ends at FY2018). Filed values in the FY2025 10-K: $1,199,103,000 (FY2023), $1,329,747,000 (FY2024), $1,429,980,000 (FY2025). The engine applies this single value to every missing period; the value used is the median of the three filed years (the FY2024 figure). Against the true per-year figures it overstates FY2023 capex by $130,644,000 (conservative direction — lowers that year's OE) and understates FY2025 capex by $100,233,000 (flatters the latest year — noted, not hidden; the verdict does not change on the true figures, since OCF minus capex minus SBC is negative in all three years either way). Excluded, deliberately: 'Acquisitions of utility systems, net' ($57,004,000 in FY2025, same statement) is system M&A presented separately by the filer, not capex.

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0000078128-26-000050), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Property, plant and equipment additions, including the debt component of allowance for funds used during construction': $(1,429,980) thousand for FY2025, $(1,329,747) thousand for FY2024 and $(1,199,103) thousand for FY2023; the identical three figures are reported as consolidated capital expenditures in the same 10-K's segment note (Note 19) and are tagged in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings. The override value is the median of the three filed years.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
note: No positive NORMALIZED (3-yr median) conservative owner's earnings — OE DCF not supportable on numbers alone. If the latest year alone is positive, that is a flag to investigate, not a pass. F sub-type: no cash generation (OCF - capex is not positive).

override_impact.basis: engine-native normalized base (median of last 3 FY) and weighted IRR, DCF run both ways (zero-fill baseline vs with-override); a --base-oe-ps TTM base is excluded from both sides — its override effect shows in ttm.py output
